scope: Official SQLite WASM documentation, the official sqlite/sqlite-wasm package, and SQLite 3.54.1 source

claims.claim: The official npm package wraps SQLite WASM as an ES module and adds TypeScript types without modifying the underlying WASM implementation
The official npm package currently supports Node.js only for in-memory databases without persistence
claims.notes: Do not reuse browser OPFS examples as Node persistence.

claims.claim: OPFS is available only in Worker-thread contexts, not the main UI thread
The standard OPFS VFS requires SharedArrayBuffer and COOP/COEP response headers
claims.notes: COEP require-corp or applicable credentialless mode; COOP same-origin.

claims.claim: The opfs-wl VFS was added in 3.53.0 and uses Web Locks, requiring Atomics.waitAsync
opfs-sahpool avoids COOP/COEP and offers high OPFS throughput but does not provide transparent multi-instance concurrency
claims.notes: Multi-instance sharing requires explicit application-level coordination.

claims.claim: kvvfs stores a database in localStorage or sessionStorage, is main-thread-only in its primary implementation, and supports one database per storage object
claims.notes: Typical storage limits are small, around 5MB.

claims.claim: Worker1 and Promiser APIs are deprecated as of 2026-04-15 and are discouraged for new applications
An oo1.DB instance corresponds to a sqlite3* database connection and must be closed after use
OPFS locking requires short transactions and clients to handle SQLITE_BUSY under contention
WASMFS + OPFS requires a custom build and is not part of the canonical sqlite3.wasm build
A single Worker message should contain the full transaction when using an asynchronous message interface
claims.notes: The course demo uses a synchronous OO1 API inside an application-owned Worker.
